result.title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents tackle complex tasks through reasoning and interaction with external environments. Agent skills provide persistent, transferable capabilities that guide task planning, inform contextual decisions, support tool use, and enable executable procedures. Yet existing skill-evolution methods largely organize knowledge around skill artifacts, overlooking the functional heterogeneity within individual skills and its implications for knowledge maintenance and use. Inspired by cognitive science, we propose Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), which evolves a unified skill through four functionally distinct yet coordinated components: Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script. CDSE extracts evidence-grounded semantic gradients from successful and failed trajectories, consolidates them by functional role, and applies component-specific updates and validation with cross-component coordination and adaptive invocation. An analysis of 500 top-ranked skill packages shows that 96.8% contain knowledge spanning at least two functional roles. Across six benchmarks, three agent models, and two execution harnesses, CDSE achieves the highest scores in all 36 settings, improving over the Base agent by 7.6 percentage points and the strongest competing method in each setting by 2.6 points on average. Ablation studies further support the importance of functional differentiation and adaptive invocation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CDSE，把 LLM agent 的统一技能按功能拆成 Meta、Experience、Tool、Script 四类组件，从成功与失败轨迹中抽取有证据支撑的「语义梯度」并按功能归类，做组件化更新、验证与自适应调用，在六个基准的 36 个设定上取得最优。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 agent 工作，但其「从成败轨迹中提取证据并按功能分工更新、自适应调用」的思路，可能为 LVR 的轨迹训练、贡献分配以及何时调用 latent 模块提供可核查的方法线索。
